concepts.title: Universal Law of Gravitation
concepts.body: Every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. For example, the Earth pulls you towards its center, keeping you grounded.

concepts.title: Free Fall and Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)
concepts.body: When an object falls under the influence of gravity alone, it is said to be in free fall. The acceleration due to gravity (g) is approximately 9.8 m/s^2 and is the same for all objects, regardless of their mass. For instance, a feather and a hammer would fall at the same rate in a vacuum.

concepts.title: Mass vs Weight
concepts.body: Mass is the amount of matter in an object and remains constant everywhere, while weight is the force exerted on an object due to gravity and changes with the value of g. For example, your mass is the same on Earth and the Moon, but your weight is less on the Moon due to its weaker gravity.

formulas.title: Universal Law of Gravitation Formula
formulas.body: F = G x m1 x m2 / r^2 (F in newton N, m in kg, r in m, G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2). Here, F is the gravitational force, G is the gravitational constant, m1 and m2 are the masses of the two objects, and r is the distance between their centers. This formula is used to calculate the gravitational force between two objects.

formulas.title: Weight Formula
formulas.body: W = m x g (W in newton N, m in kg, g in m/s^2). Here, W is the weight, m is the mass of the object, and g is the acceleration due to gravity. This formula is used to calculate the weight of an object based on its mass and the gravitational acceleration.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you jump, you come back down to the ground because of the gravitational force exerted by the Earth. This force pulls you towards the center of the Earth.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: Satellites orbiting the Earth are kept in their paths by the gravitational force between the Earth and the satellite. This force acts as the centripetal force required for their circular motion.

mcqs.question: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity (g) on Earth?
mcqs.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s^2. This is a fundamental constant used in physics calculations.

mcqs.question: If the mass of an object is 10 kg, what is its weight on Earth?
mcqs.explanation: Weight is calculated using the formula W = m x g. Here, m = 10 kg and g = 9.8 m/s^2. Therefore, W = 10 x 9.8 = 98 N. The other options are incorrect because they either use incorrect values for g or m.

mcqs.question: Two objects of masses 5 kg and 10 kg are placed 2 meters apart. What is the gravitational force between them?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula F = G x m1 x m2 / r^2, where G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2, m1 = 5 kg, m2 = 10 kg, and r = 2 m, we get F = 6.67 x 10^-11 x 5 x 10 / 4 = 8.34 x 10^-10 N. The other options are incorrect because they either use incorrect values for G, m1, m2, or r.
